definitions.explanation: The state of being destroyed or severely damaged.

examples.japanese: {戦争|せんそう}で{町|まち}が{荒廃|こうはい}した。
examples.english: The town was devastated by war.

examples.japanese: {荒廃|こうはい}した{土地|とち}を{再生|さいせい}する。
{大|おお}きな{地震|じしん}の{後|あと}、{街|まち}は{荒廃|こうはい}し、{住民|じゅうみん}は{避難|ひなん}を{余儀|よぎ}なくされた。
examples.english: After the major earthquake, the city was devastated and residents were forced to evacuate.

examples.japanese: {心|こころ}の{荒廃|こうはい}が{問題|もんだい}だ。
examples.english: The decay of the spirit is a problem.

examples.japanese: {人|ひと}が{住|す}まなくなり、{建物|たてもの}が{荒廃|こうはい}していった。
examples.english: People stopped living there, and the buildings fell into decay.

examples.japanese: {経済|けいざい}の{悪化|あっか}にともなって{社会|しゃかい}{全体|ぜんたい}に{荒廃|こうはい}が{広|ひろ}がり、{犯罪|はんざい}も{増|ふ}えた。
examples.english: As the economy worsened, decay spread throughout society, and crime also increased.

notes:
Can refer to physical destruction or moral/spiritual decline.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{荒廃|こうはい}する (to fall into ruin)
・{荒廃|こうはい}した{町|まち}/{土地|とち} (ruined town/land)
・{国土|こくど}の{荒廃|こうはい} (devastation of the land)
・{心|こころ}の{荒廃|こうはい} (spiritual decay)
・{荒廃|こうはい}を{招|まね}く (to bring about ruin)

HOMOPHONE:
・{後輩|こうはい} - junior (in school or work)

These two words are both read こうはい but have completely different meanings.

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{廃墟|はいきょ} (ruins)
・{衰退|すいたい} (decline, decay)
・{荒|あ}れる (to become desolate)
